one_liner: Node 19.7 (V8) runs a Pall-style fannkuch-redux 1.38x faster than the suite's plainer C program; the gap is algorithmic, not a JIT win.
what_it_does: A single row of kostya/jit-benchmarks, a 2023 Docker-based suite comparing JIT and interpreter implementations of Ruby, Python, Lua, JavaScript and PHP against C and Crystal on Benchmarks Game programs. The fannkuch-redux workload enumerates all 10! permutations, counts pancake flips per permutation and prints a checksum (73196) and the maximum flip count (38). fannkuchredux/test.js is Isaac Gouy's transliteration of Mike Pall's Lua program, run with plain `node test.js 10 5`; there is no library to adopt, only a comparison of two different programs.
how_it_is_fast: Mostly by doing less work. The JS program caches the first element, writes q[q0]=q0 directly instead of moving it through the flip, reverses only q[1..q0-1] and skips the reverse when q0 < 3, skips the copy entirely when the permutation already starts with 0, and steps permutations with an alternating swap instead of a full prefix rotation. The C program (Mazurov/Piché, Java-derived, VLA arrays) copies the whole permutation every time, reverses the full prefix including element 0 on each flip and rotates perm1[0..r] for each new permutation. An agent count of array element moves in the two algorithms at n=10 gives 168.4M for the C program against 118.8M for the JS one, 1.42x more work, which matches the measured 1.38x time ratio (agent instrumentation in Python, both reproduce checksum 73196 and max flips 38; a proxy, not a timing). V8's TurboFan then runs the cheaper algorithm at native-like speed on small-integer arrays.
when_to_use: As a data point that V8's optimising tier can run tight integer array loops within the same range as gcc -O3 output, once warm.
When choosing between JS engines for compute kernels: in the same table Node 0.15 s beats GraalVM JS (0.18-0.19 s) and LuaJIT running the same Pall algorithm (0.27 s).
When porting a hot integer loop from JavaScript to C or C++: carry the algorithmic tricks over, or the native port can come out slower, as this C program does.
Teaching or reviewing cross-language benchmarks: a clear example of an algorithm mismatch masquerading as a language result.
when_not_to_use: As evidence that JavaScript beats C or C++: the suite's own Cython row, gcc -O3 compiling a closer-to-Pall flip loop with the lookahead trick and swap-based permutation step, runs in 0.129 s, faster than Node's 0.152 s.
As a statement about current engines: numbers are from 2023-02-28 with Node 19.7.0 and gcc 12.2.0; the benchmark code has not changed since March 2023 and nothing was re-run.
Memory-constrained use: Node's process peaks at 45.4 MB against 0.9 MB for the C program.
Short single-shot runs: Best T excludes start-up (about 0.24 s to reach the started marker in Node's container) and the slowest of Node's five in-process runs was 0.183 s.
Multi-threaded or SIMD work: the suite is deliberately single-threaded and avoids low-level hacks, so it says nothing about the Benchmarks Game's fastest parallel C fannkuch programs.

integration.dependencies: Node.js 19.7.0 (built from the suite's docker/nodejs image); the C baseline needs only libc
integration.min_toolchain: Node.js 19.7.0 as measured; the program uses only Array, Date, console and process.argv, so any recent Node runs it
integration.platforms: Measured on x86-64 (AMD Ryzen 7 3800X, Docker on Ubuntu 22.10); the README says the suite also runs on aarch64 (tested on Apple M1), but no aarch64 results are published

gotchas: Algorithm mismatch behind the numbers: test.c is the Mazurov/Piché Java-derived program and test.js is Pall's Lua algorithm, so the README's promise of 'one algorithm' does not hold here. By agent count the C program moves 1.42x more array elements at n=10 (168.4M vs 118.8M), about the same as the 1.38x time gap; Crystal's port of the C algorithm takes 0.19 s and LuaJIT's run of the Pall algorithm 0.27 s, so neither language nor JIT explains the Node row alone.

Different clocks with different resolution: C reports clock() process CPU time printed with %.2f (10 ms steps, so 'C 0.21 s' covers 0.205-0.215 s), Node reports Date wall time in milliseconds (0.152 s); the ratio is therefore 1.35x to 1.41x, not a precise 1.4x.

Best T is the minimum of five in-process runs (results/amd64/round_1.yml: Node 0.152-0.183 s, C 0.21-0.22 s), so V8 warm-up and on-stack replacement are mostly excluded; the earlier round_0.yml run agrees (Node 0.148 s, C 0.21 s).

The harness checks output only at n=5 (expected checksum 11 and 'Pfannkuchen(5) = 7'), not at the measured n=10; the agent re-ran both algorithms in Python and they agree at n=10 (73196, 38), so no correctness problem was found.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Do not pick it as a performance claim: among the same suite's catalogued rows, Node regex-dna (5.3x over C using PCRE without its JIT) and LuaJIT k-nucleotide (2.7x over substr-heavy std::unordered_map C++) also rest on weak baselines but at least use comparable algorithms, while benchLANG and LangArena entries measure one shared algorithm per language with current toolchains. Cite this row only to show how an algorithm swap can flip a language ranking.
verified_claims_summary: On an AMD Ryzen 7 3800X under Docker on Ubuntu 22.10 (round 1, 2023-02-28), fannkuch-redux at n=10 took 0.152 s for test.js on Node 19.7.0 against 0.21 s for test.c built with gcc 12.2.0 -O3 -march=native -fomit-frame-pointer -funroll-loops, each the best of five in-process runs timed by the program itself (about 1.38x, derived from page data and results/amd64/round_1.yml). The two programs use different algorithms, and a gcc -O3 build of a closer-to-Pall algorithm (the Cython row, 0.129 s) beats Node.
status_note: MIT-licensed, 105 stars, 69 commits and 6 open issues; benchmark code and results unchanged since 2023 (the only 2026 commit adds a README link to the author's newer LangArena suite), so treat it as a frozen 2023 snapshot and use LangArena or kostya/benchmarks for current numbers.
